thread.title: Iberia suspends Madrid-Havana flights amid US fuel blockade and reduced demand
thread.title_full: Iberia suspends Madrid-Havana flights amid US fuel blockade and reduced demand

author: golden state today
title: Iberia suspends Madrid-Havana flights amid US fuel blockade and reduced demand
text:
Iberia began a suspension of its route between Adolfo Suárez Madrid Barajas Airport in Spain and Havana José Martí International Airport in Cuba on June 1, with plans to resume service in late October. The Spanish national airline said the decision reflects challenging conditions caused by the impacts of the US fuel blockade on Cuba, which has led to dwindling supplies and a reduction in airline operations to the country.
According to Newsweek, Iberia experienced a drop in demand for its Cuban flights, prompting this hiatus. The carrier had gradually decreased its frequency from three weekly rotations in April to two by June before ceasing operations entirely for the summer season. In an April statement, Iberia said that “since February 9, (…) it [had been] necessary to perform a technical stop in Santo Domingo for refueling on return flights to Madrid” due to fuel shortages in Cuba. Passengers holding bookings between June 1 and October 24 are permitted to switch their routes from Havana to Miami, Mexico City, Panama City or Santo Domingo: “Route changes from HAV to MIA, PTY, SDQ, or MEX are permitted on the same or nearby dates to the original booking. Transfers to/from the alternative airports are not covered by the airline.”
The withdrawal of Iberia from this route affects not only travel between Spain and Cuba but also reduces options for passengers traveling between Europe and Cuba overall. According to data provided by Cirium, Air China is one of four airlines operating between Europe and Cuba this June; it serves Havana from Madrid as part of a longer Beijing route with eight planned rotations this month. Air Europa scheduled twelve rotations on Madrid-Havana during June as well.
Cuban flag carrier Cubana will operate nine flights from Madrid this month—four nonstop and five via Santiago de Cuba—using Ilyushin Il-96 aircraft instead of Boeing 787s used by other carriers. Additionally, Neos will connect Milan and Rome with Havana via La Romana using Boeing 787s.
Iberia’s provisional plan is set for resumption at the end of October when it intends three Airbus A330-operated rotations at first before increasing frequency through November and December if conditions allow.
